summary: Add isolated service tests, controllable time and guidance checked against the installed Effect APIs.
description: Add Effect-focused testing practices and guidance checked against installed APIs. Tests use real service layers with fresh state, controlled clocks and explicit assertions for failures and defects. An API reference the agent writes records the installed release's service, schema and runtime conventions. The stack still owns application architecture, services, configuration and logging; this fragment supports developing and testing them.
seoDescription: Effect testing guidance with fresh service layers, virtual time and an installed-API reference for coding agents working on TypeScript programs.

projectExamples.title: Timed API service tests
projectExamples.description: Test custom retry or timeout behavior directly with provided layers and TestClock. Keep HTTP boundary checks in the stack's real request harness.

projectExamples.title: Isolated command service tests
projectExamples.description: Add tests proving separate CLI invocations do not share service state. Use real layers and stub only external boundaries.

plain.whatItIs: Test helpers and guidance for coding assistants working on code written with Effect, a TypeScript library for structuring services and errors.
goodAt: Testing services with a controlled clock, so tests skip real waiting
Checking that failures and unexpected crashes are reported as intended
Giving coding assistants reference notes that match the installed Effect version
notGoodAt: Choosing how a whole app is organized; the base project recipe makes that choice.

requests: test timed operations by advancing a clock instead of sleeping
keep service state isolated between tests while using real layers
